directive: Uphold the REVISE while preserving the field-novel kernel: legally realized, relatively open, two-sided selective-label refinement. Demote thm:sharp-selective-label-interval to a corollary of the substantive finite-response converse, and demote prop:z-blind-containment to a one-line coarsening lemma. Replace the abstract 32-column certificate by a complete specification of (S, J0, e, Q, c, rho) and an injective table i -> (s,z,(a_c),(y_c)); verify every listed type satisfies all four SLCC restrictions, identify its observable row and target value, and prove that every other legal type/observable cell in the full model cannot change the four optima and that p^(32,o) lies in relint(O), not merely in the relative interior of a displayed submatrix. Preserve and verify the arithmetic L=p1+p2, U=p1+p2+p4, L_blind=p1, U_blind=1, yielding [1/2,3/4] versus [1/4,1] and [397/800,601/800] versus [99/400,1]. Repair prop:trialed-policy-reduction: ordinary identification requires c_e(s)=c_j*(s) for all s; A_c=1 only makes Z fully observed and does not identify a distinct untrialed configuration. Correct Duarte et al. to Section 6 and Appendix E, acknowledge generic confidence-region propagation as prior art, and present the finite-sample theorem as an application/implementation corollary. Do not require a global necessary-and-sufficient facet criterion in this revision: once the full-model realization and actual relative-interiority hold, the two strict gaps 199/800 plus continuity of polyhedral value functions supply the relative-open neighborhood. If all legal columns cannot be controlled or actual relint(O) cannot be established, do not claim the strict-refinement kernel.
